issue.title: No drop_community is added to advertised IPv6 routes

failure.body:
**Description**
After the BGP Allow List feature is introduced, the drop_community should be added to advertised routes that are not on allow list when default_action is "permit". However, the drop_community `"5056:12345"` is not added to IPv6 routes.

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. By default, default_action of BGP allow list is "permit" and the allow list is empty. All the routes advertised by SONIC should have community "5056:12345".
2. Check the routes on neighbors. The IPv6 routes received from SONiC do not have drop_community in community list. Only IPv4 routes have drop_community.
```
ARISTA01T2#show ip bgp <IP>/25
BGP routing table information for VRF default
Router identifier <IP>, local AS number 65200
BGP routing table entry for <IP>/25
 Paths: 1 available
  65100 64001
    <IP> from <IP> (<IP>)
      Origin IGP, metric 0, localpref 100, IGP metric 1, weight 0, received <IPV6> ago, valid, external, best
      Community: 5060:12345
      Rx SAFI: Unicast
ARISTA01T2#
ARISTA01T2#show ipv6 bgp 20c0:a800::/64
BGP routing table information for VRF default
Router identifier <IP>, local AS number 65200
BGP routing table entry for 20c0:a800::/64
 Paths: 1 available
  65100 64001
    fc00::1 from fc00::1 (<IP>)
      Origin IGP, metric 0, localpref 100, IGP metric 1, weight 0, received <IPV6> ago, valid, external, best
      Rx SAFI: Unicast
```
3.

**Describe the results you received:**
When default_action of BGP allow list is "permit", SONiC does not add drop_community to advertised IPv6 routes that are not on allow list.

**Describe the results you expected:**
The SONiC switch should add drop_community to both IPv4 and IPv6 routes that are not on allow list when default_action of BGP allow list is `"permit"`.

**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**

The reason is that SONiC has an extra rule for route-map `FROM_BGP_PEER_V6`:
```
route-map FROM_BGP_PEER_V6 permit 1
 set ipv6 next-hop prefer-global
```
This rule has the highest priority. When this rule is hit, the IPv6 routes are permitted and then advertised to other peers. Rest rules of route-map `FROM_BGP_PEER_V6` are not hit. Including the rule for adding drop_community:
```
route-map FROM_BGP_PEER_V6 permit 2
 call ALLOW_LIST_DEPLOYMENT_ID_0_V6
 on-match next

route-map ALLOW_LIST_DEPLOYMENT_ID_0_V6 permit 65535
 set community 5060:12345 additive
```

resolution.title: [bgpcfgd]: Add on-match next rule for set ipv6 next-hop prefer-global
resolution.description:
**- Why I did it**
Without the rule, IPv6 route-map entries were skipped.
**- How I did it**
Added 'on-match next' rule after 'set ipv6 next-hop prefer-global.
Updated a test to check that we have 'on-match next' rule with the 'set ipv6 next-hop prefer-global'

**- How to verify it**
Build an image. Run on your dut. Add a route-map entry after 'set ipv6 next-hop prefer-global'. Check that the route-map entry works
**- Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)**

- [ ] 201811
- [ ] 201911
- [x] 202006

**- Description for the changelog**

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**
